name: Subject and Reference
title: Subject and Reference
text:
SUBJECT: REPLY TO YOUR NOTICE DATED {{original_notice_date}} RECEIVED BY MY CLIENT ON {{original_notice_received_date}}.

REF: Your notice bearing reference {{original_notice_reference}}.

legal_basis.note: An admission is a statement suggesting an inference as to a fact in issue, and is evidence against the party who makes it. This restates the principle formerly in S.17 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872; the corresponding section of the Adhiniyam must be confirmed against the bare Act.

statutory_reference: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 - section to be confirmed
authoring_note: Recording the date of receipt, as distinct from the date the notice bears, matters wherever a statutory period runs from receipt. It also puts the sender to proof if they later assert an earlier service date.
statute_currency: CITATION OUT OF DATE. The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 was repealed with effect from 1 July 2024 by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. The principle relied on here survives the repeal, but the SECTION NUMBER does not carry across - the Adhiniyam renumbered throughout. Published correspondence tables circulating online disagree with one another, so the advocate must map this citation against the bare Adhiniyam text rather than a table, and record the confirmed section here.
